ai.description: This lizard reaches 10–12 cm snout-vent length. It is olive-brown with dark crossbands and a distinct white stripe along the flanks. A prominent, serrated dorsal crest extends from the neck to the tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Calotes maria* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, black-bordered white or pale spot located just above the tympanum, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Calotes maria* inhabits the subtropical broadleaf forests and montane regions of the Khasi Hills, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Khasi Hills forest lizard is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on tree trunks or rocks to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calotes maria* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Calotes maria* is endemic to the Northeast Indian states of Meghalaya, Nagaland, and Mizoram, typically inhabiting montane forests at elevations above 1,000 meters.
